recent_posts.title: 7 common Databricks mistakes that increase costs
recent_posts.summary: Databricks costs can spiral quickly without proper management. Common expensive mistakes include running unnecessary or overly frequent jobs, oversizing compute clusters, misusing Photon optimization, forgetting to enable auto-stop on SQL warehouses, and neglecting query and storage optimizations. The article shares practical lessons from reducing Databricks costs by 50% in weeks, emphasizing that starting with minimal resources and scaling up as needed, along with regular monitoring and optimization, can prevent wasteful spending on compute and storage.

recent_posts.title: React Native Upgrade: How to Tackle the Mission
recent_posts.summary: A detailed technical guide documenting the upgrade process from React Native 0.75.4 to 0.77.2, driven by the need to integrate the HaloC SDK. The post covers version selection rationale, breaking changes assessment, dependency management strategy, and step-by-step implementation including iOS/Android native updates. Key challenges included navigation library major version jumps (react-native-screens 2.x to 4.x), animation system compatibility, and edge-to-edge enforcement on Android. The author shares real-world issues encountered, such as TouchableOpacity deprecation, Metro logging changes, and UI overlapping problems, along with practical solutions and rollback planning strategies.

recent_posts.title: Evaluating Python 3.13's true parallelism capabilities
recent_posts.summary: Python 3.13 introduces the ability to disable the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), allowing true parallelism within a single Python process. Benchmarks demonstrate significant performance improvements with this feature, although it adds some overhead to single-threaded processes. The free-threaded mode remains experimental and may require updates to C extensions and careful maintenance of thread-safety.

recent_posts.title: Building a Custom Swipe to Delete Component in React Native
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build a customizable swipe-to-delete component in React Native from scratch using the react-native-gesture-handler and react-native-reanimated libraries. This guide covers setting up shared values for animations, handling dynamic layouts, implementing swipe gestures, managing position resets and deletions, and adding smooth animations for a seamless user experience.

recent_posts.title: I Want to Fly, But I Don’t Know How: Navigating the Early Days of a Junior Developer
recent_posts.summary: Starting a career as a junior software developer comes with its challenges. Key tips include using AI as a supplemental tool rather than a crutch, understanding tasks thoroughly before diving in, leveraging the fresh perspective juniors bring, documenting your learning journey to retain knowledge, and staying curious by asking questions. These strategies can help junior developers grow and thrive in their roles.

recent_posts.title: How to Work Around Next.js Limitation of Importing CSS Outside the Main File Using Styled-Components?
recent_posts.summary: The post addresses a common issue in Next.js where global CSS can't be imported from files other than the main App file. It provides a solution using styled-components to import CSS from third-party libraries. The solution involves creating a styled component that serves as a placeholder for the global CSS and using a Node.js script to inject the actual CSS at build time.

recent_posts.title: Memory Leak Profiling and Pinpointing for Node.js
recent_posts.summary: We identified and fixed a memory leak in a Nest.js application running on Kubernetes, which was caused by open handles not being properly closed during proxy requests to Grafana. Using Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring, along with custom modifications to the wtf-node dependency, we pinpointed the issue and adjusted the middleware to prevent the memory leak. Key steps include integrating prom-client with Grafana and using wtf-node to diagnose active handle issues.

recent_posts.title: Redefined Systems Resiliency 101: Do’s and Don’ts
recent_posts.summary: Resiliency in systems means ensuring that a system never fails, no matter the circumstances. This includes maintaining full functionality despite system and software updates, dependency and compatibility issues, resource limitations, hardware failures, and procedural errors. Key strategies include backward and forward compatibility for APIs and databases, safe autoscaling, active-active or active-passive data centers for failover, and meaningful circuit breakers. It's crucial for system leadership to prioritize plans addressing potential failures and have robust engineering and risk management practices in place.

recent_posts.title: Spring Cloud Gateway MVC — Migration from Reactive one
recent_posts.summary: Spring Cloud Gateway MVC simplifies API gateway management by eliminating the need for Reactive programming. Leveraging Spring Boot 3.2.x and JDK 21’s Virtual Threads, it offers a more intuitive approach to routing, filtering, error handling, and security. Developers transitioning from Reactive to MVC can expect smoother integration and improved maintainability, despite some current limitations and unresolved issues.

recent_posts.title: Harnessing the Power of Spring Cloud Config for Microservices Using Azure Data Explorer as Backend
recent_posts.summary: Explore the benefits of using Spring Cloud Config for managing configurations in microservices applications. Learn about the advantages of centralized configuration, the types of configurations that can be stored, and how to customize Spring Cloud Config to fetch configurations from Azure Data Explorer.
